messages:
kev: Noticed a weird class of funcall JSON failures in the nova-q int4 canary. ~1.6% of mirror calls show truncated suffixes, but many shards have complementary fragments (partial endings).

lia: Complementary fragments? like different replicas returning different suffix bits?

kev: Exactly. Because we mirror to multiple replicas for low-latency hedged reads, some replicas cut earlier, some cut a few bytes later. If you stitch them lexicographically you sometimes recover a valid JSON.

sam: Whoa. That's interesting. Could we run a lightweight consensus stitcher before applying repairs? I.e., if 2/3 replicas agree on last N bytes, use that as final tail, otherwise mark truncated.

marta: I like the idea but we must be conservative: do NOT invent required keys. Consensus stitch only for suffix bytes and optional leaf arrays/strings. Also record which schema paths were affected.

kev: Proposed flow: for mirrored/hedged requests, collect final chunk from each replica -> run byte-level majority vote on last 128 bytes -> if majority yields valid UTF-8 and closes JSON, accept; else fall back to repair heuristic gated by schema-path whitelist.\n
lia: Telemetry to add: consensus_success_rate, repaired_vs_consensus_count, parse_failures_post_consensus, average_stitch_latency. Also tag requests where stitch changed token boundary.

ops-bot: alert created: canary-consensus-parse-failures > 0.4% sustained for 5m.

sam: Runtime changes: (1) hedged-collector exposes final_chunk[] per-replica, (2) stitcher module does majority-by-byte, (3) short-circuit repair whitelist for optional leaves only. I'll prototype the stitcher. ETA 6h.

marta: Add a policy: if stitch produces content that fills in a required field path (e.g., /intent), reject and escalate to dev leads.

kev: Unit test idea: simulate 3 replica chunks where each missing different trailing bytes; assert stitch recovers valid JSON and that required keys remain intact. Also test cases where majority is inconsistent -> ensure we fail safe (return structured truncated error).

lia: SDK change: when we detect a structured-truncated error, include a retry token so callers can re-invoke with the same context but force non-streaming mode. That helps clients avoid partial streaming ambiguity.

infra-bot: rolling audit log: mirrored request ids will be recorded to /var/logs/consensus-stitch/6632104321.log (redacted).

kev: Plan: pause further rollout until stitcher + telemetry live for canary subset (10% traffic). Run 200k mirror A/B comparing baseline float vs int4+stitch. If residual parse_failures < 0.25% and stitch false-positive < 0.05%, proceed.

marta: Also add guard: max_stitch_bytes=256 and only run stitch if at least 3 replicas responded.

sam: I'll open PR for stitcher + unit tests. kev, lia please review.

kev: Actions: sam implement stitcher (ETA 6h), lia add SDK retry token + tests (ETA 8h), marta add schema-path whitelist + alert (ETA 3h). I'll coordinate A/B run once merged.

kev: dropping a redacted token dump for kernel team at /infra/bench/novaq/trace-6632104321.log

lia: Nice—this keeps us conservative but gives a non-invasive path to recover many truncated cases. Good job. :rocket:
